2606.04045.COMMENT: Defines Bayes-sufficient and Bayes-minimal representations as the loss-dependent minimal information needed for Bayes-optimal prediction.
2606.04045.HOTSPOT_PAPER_COMMENT: Broadly important today: Defines Bayes-sufficient and Bayes-minimal representations as the loss-dependent minimal information needed for Bayes-optimal prediction.
2606.04045.TOPIC_MATCH_COMMENT: This is directly about what information representations must preserve, offering a clean theoretical framework for sufficiency and minimality in supervised representation learning.
2606.04045.abstract: Representation learning is often described as preserving the information in an input that is relevant for prediction. This work asks what relevance means for a fixed supervised decision problem. A representation is defined to be Bayes-sufficient for a joint distribution and loss if some prediction head can use it to implement a Bayes-optimal action rule. This makes the target information loss-dependent. In the almost-surely unique Bayes-action case, the relevant object is a Bayes quotient, which identifies inputs that require the same Bayes-optimal action. 2606.04045.title: Bayes-Sufficient Representations in Supervised Learning

2606.04050.COMMENT: Introduces quasi-continuous bit-width control through lift-then-project quantization with hardware-friendly decoding.
2606.04050.HOTSPOT_PAPER_COMMENT: Broadly important today: Introduces quasi-continuous bit-width control through lift-then-project quantization with hardware-friendly decoding.
2606.04050.TOPIC_MATCH_COMMENT: Quantization is the core contribution, and the continuous bit-width mechanism is a strong foundational efficiency idea rather than routine compression.
2606.04050.abstract: Existing quantization methods are fundamentally limited by rigid, integer-based bit-widths (e.g., 2, 3-bit), resulting in a ``deployment gap" where Large Language Models cannot be optimally fitted to specific memory budgets. To bridge this gap, we introduce LiftQuant, a novel framework that enables continuous bit-width control for true Pareto-optimal deployment. The core innovation is a ``lift-then-project" mechanism which approximates low-dimensional weight vectors by projecting a simple 1-bit lattice from a higher-dimensional ``lifted" space. 2606.04050.title: LiftQuant: Continuous Bit-Width LLM via Dimensional Lifting and Projection

2606.04120.abstract: Conversational agents that serve as lifelong companions must maintain persistent memory across all interactions. However, simply expanding context windows with raw retrieval degrades reasoning quality, while training memory agents via standard reinforcement learning creates a severe credit assignment bottleneck in a multi-stage pipeline. To solve this, we introduce SALIMORY, a framework that trains a single language model to manage a cognitively-structured memory-spanning user facts, preferences, and working memory.
